summary: Verified iOS/Safari native-gray select fix via computed-style checks across mobile + desktop viewports, teacher & student pages, and light mode. All targeted selects render themed (appearance:none, dark bg, light text, SVG chevron on left) with selected option text visible. gen-grade-select in QuestionBank AI dialog now correctly uses input-field class (previous iteration's minor issue is resolved). All regression checks pass.

issues: Grade select in light mode renders bg-color rgb(248,250,252) (from html.mode-light .glass-modal select rule at index.css:755-761) instead of the spec's #FBF6E7 (html.mode-light select.input-field at :649-651). The .glass-modal-scoped rule wins by specificity. Result is still light-bg + dark-text (rgb(15,23,42)) with visible chevron SVG — visually correct but not the exact cream palette. Low priority.

action_items: OPTIONAL/LOW: Align light-mode select bg inside .glass-modal to the cream palette (#FBF6E7) for full theme consistency — currently overridden to slate-50 by .glass-modal light-mode block.
critical_code_review_comments: select.input-field CSS block at index.css:354-368 correctly forces -webkit-appearance:none !important + custom chevron on the LEFT (RTL) — the definitive fix for iOS Safari's native gray rendering.
gen-grade-select in QuestionBank.jsx now confirmed to have class='input-field' (iteration_2's remaining inconsistency is resolved).

Pre-existing React DOM-nesting warnings (<span> as child of <select>/<option>) still pollute the console — appears to come from a devtools/instrumentation wrapper. Non-blocking but noisy; recommend disabling instrumentation in production build.
